  "summary": "The brief's raw URL and its directory URL both return 404 at tag 26.6.4. The handler lives at python/unblob/handlers/filesystem/squashfs.py (raw returns HTTP 200). Fetched 2026-10-26T06:17:04Z; tag 26.6.4 is commit 1fcc7a0a. The file is 590 lines, 19842 B, sha256 2d7b901b54e2ad28c28df2cbbdaeb4bcedb58670fb4c4478f9578a0dd5599287, and its git blob sha matches the GitHub API tree entry. A copy is saved in the artifacts dir.

Dispatch is by magic pattern. squashfs_v4_le matches `68 73 71 73 [24] 04 00` (L454-466). squashfs_v4_be matches `73 71 73 68 [24] 00 04` (L513-525) and sets `EXTRACTOR = SquashFSExtractor(4, 0x73717368)` at L527. The v4_le handler sets no extractor and inherits the version-3 one (L75), which doesn't matter because a little-endian magic always takes the `-le` branch.

SquashFSExtractor (L24-69) decides endianness at extract time and shells out through `Command`. For big-endian v4 it runs `sasquatch-v4be`, adding `-be` unless the header looks like AVM (`bytes_used == mkfs_time`, L48-50). Other cases run plain `sasquatch -be` or `-le`. get_dependencies (L68-69) always lists both executables. A standard big-endian carrier (K1-K4) therefore runs `sasquatch-v4be -be -no-exit-code -f -d <out> <in>`.

The frozen claim wording conflicts with this source: R38-C1 says "no external extractor dependency" and that stock unblob handles big-endian v4 without one. The source shows the handler always shells out to `sasquatch-v4be`, and 26.6.4 has no in-process squashfs reader. ~/.local/bin/sasquatch-v4be exists on the host (the L1 installed it), so the receipts may have used it. Check K*/after.json for which binary ran, or for an ExtractorDependencyNotFoundReport, before admitting that wording. The SOURCES row can back the dispatch and the `sasquatch-v4be -be` invocation, but not "no external extractor".

The report has the located quotes with line numbers, a draft SOURCES row and the directory listing. I only fetched files and read them; nothing was installed or run, and scratch is removed."
}
